say.sl: **It was Jack who found her.** (Jack je bil tisti, ki jo je našel.) Kar je pomembno, stoji v sredini: **It was** + oseba + **who**. Prav je tudi **that**: **It was Jack that found her.** Ostane ednina: **It was Jack and Meg who found her.** Ljudje rečejo tudi *It was Jack what found her* in *It were*; v pisanju **who** in **was**.
say.de: **It was Jack who found her.** (Es war Jack, der sie gefunden hat.) Was zählt, steht in der Mitte: **It was** + die Person + **who**. Auch **that** ist richtig: **It was Jack that found her.** Es bleibt Singular, anders als im Deutschen: **It was Jack and Meg who found her.** Man sagt auch *It was Jack what found her* und *It were*; geschrieben **who** und **was**.
say.it: **It was Jack who found her.** (È stato Jack a trovarla.) Ciò che conta sta in mezzo: **It was** + la persona + **who**. Va bene anche **that**: **It was Jack that found her.** Resta al singolare, non come *sono stati*: **It was Jack and Meg who found her.** Si dice anche *It was Jack what found her* e *It were*; per iscritto **who** e **was**.
say.en: **It was Jack who found her.** What matters goes in the middle: **It was** + the person + **who**. **that** is right too: **It was Jack that found her.** It stays singular: **It was Jack and Meg who found her.** People also say *It was Jack what found her* and *It were*; writing wants **who** and **was**.

say.sl: Stvar, kraj ali čas ima **that**, samo oseba **who**: **It was the fog that stopped him.** (Ustavila ga je megla.) **It was in Keswick that we met.** **It was on Saturday that she got lost.** Tudi v sedanjiku: **It's the cold that I hate.** Tako popraviš, kar je kdo rekel narobe: ne v Penrithu, v Keswicku.
say.de: Bei einer Sache, einem Ort oder einer Zeitangabe steht **that**, nur bei einer Person **who**: **It was the fog that stopped him.** (Es war der Nebel, der ihn aufgehalten hat.) **It was in Keswick that we met.** **It was on Saturday that she got lost.** Auch im Präsens: **It's the cold that I hate.** So stellst du richtig, was jemand falsch gesagt hat: nicht in Penrith, in Keswick.
say.it: Una cosa, un luogo o un momento vogliono **that**, solo una persona **who**: **It was the fog that stopped him.** (È stata la nebbia a fermarlo.) **It was in Keswick that we met.** **It was on Saturday that she got lost.** Anche al presente: **It's the cold that I hate.** Così correggi ciò che qualcuno ha detto male: non a Penrith, a Keswick.
say.en: A thing, a place or a time takes **that**, and only a person **who**: **It was the fog that stopped him.** **It was in Keswick that we met.** **It was on Saturday that she got lost.** In the present too: **It's the cold that I hate.** It's how you put right what someone got wrong: not in Penrith, in Keswick.

say.sl: Kar je pomembno, pride zadnje: **What** + stavek + **is**, v pretekliku **was**: **What I need is a rest.** (Kar potrebujem, je počitek.) **What she needed was a cup of tea.** Enako **All I want is a quiet night.** (Vse, kar hočem, je mirna noč.) Pred **is** ni vejice, čeprav jo ima slovenščina.
say.de: Das Wichtige kommt zuletzt: **What** + Satz + **is**, in der Vergangenheit **was**: **What I need is a rest.** (Was ich brauche, ist Ruhe.) **What she needed was a cup of tea.** Ebenso **All I want is a quiet night.** (Alles, was ich will, ist eine ruhige Nacht.) Vor **is** steht kein Komma, anders als im Deutschen.
say.it: Ciò che conta viene per ultimo: **What** + frase + **is**, al passato **was**: **What I need is a rest.** (Ciò di cui ho bisogno è riposare.) **What she needed was a cup of tea.** Così anche **All I want is a quiet night.** (Tutto ciò che voglio è una notte tranquilla.) Si dice **What**, non *That*: è il *ciò che* italiano.
say.en: What matters comes last: **What** + a clause + **is**, in the past **was**: **What I need is a rest.** **What she needed was a cup of tea.** So too **All I want is a quiet night.** No comma before **is**.

say.sl: **What Jack did was ring the inn.** (Jack je naredil tole: poklical je gostilno.) Za dejanje: **What** + kdo + **did was** + osnovna oblika, preteklik je v **did**, ne v *rang*. Sme tudi **to**: **What Edna did was to walk home.** V govoru tudi **What I did was, I rang the inn.** Krajše: **All I did was ask.** (Samo {m:vprašal|f:vprašala} sem.)
say.de: **What Jack did was ring the inn.** (Jack hat einfach im Gasthaus angerufen.) Für eine Handlung: **What** + wer + **did was** + die Grundform; die Vergangenheit steckt in **did**, nicht in *rang*. Auch **to** geht: **What Edna did was to walk home.** Gesprochen auch **What I did was, I rang the inn.** Kürzer: **All I did was ask.** (Ich habe nur gefragt.)
say.it: **What Jack did was ring the inn.** (Quello che ha fatto Jack è stato chiamare la locanda.) Per un'azione: **What** + chi + **did was** + la forma base; il passato è in **did**, non in *rang*. Si può dire anche con **to**: **What Edna did was to walk home.** A voce anche **What I did was, I rang the inn.** Più breve: **All I did was ask.** (Ho solo chiesto.)
say.en: **What Jack did was ring the inn.** For an action: **What** + who + **did was** + the base form; the past is in **did**, not in *rang*. **to** may come too: **What Edna did was to walk home.** In talk also **What I did was, I rang the inn.** Shorter: **All I did was ask.**

say.sl: **do**, **does**, **did** + osnovna oblika, izgovorjeno močno, kadar kdo dvomi: **I do like your soup.** (Juha mi je res všeč.) **She did ring, twice.** **He does work hard.** Preteklik je samo v **did**: **did ring**. Tudi prijazno, gostu: **Do sit down.** (Kar sedi.)
say.de: **do**, **does**, **did** + die Grundform, betont gesprochen, wenn jemand zweifelt: **I do like your soup.** (Deine Suppe schmeckt mir wirklich.) **She did ring, twice.** **He does work hard.** Die Vergangenheit steckt nur in **did**: **did ring**. Auch herzlich, zu einem Gast: **Do sit down.** (Setz dich doch.)
say.it: **do**, **does**, **did** + la forma base, pronunciato con enfasi, quando qualcuno dubita: **I do like your soup.** (La tua zuppa mi piace davvero.) **She did ring, twice.** **He does work hard.** Il passato è solo in **did**: **did ring**. Anche con calore, a un ospite: **Do sit down.** (Siediti, dai.)
say.en: **do**, **does**, **did** + the base form, said with weight, when someone doubts it: **I do like your soup.** **She did ring, twice.** **He does work hard.** The past is only in **did**: **did ring**. Warmly too, to a guest: **Do sit down.**

say.sl: **Never have I seen such fog.** (Še nikoli nisem {m:videl|f:videla} take megle.) To moraš znati prepoznati v zgodbah in govorih: za **Never**, **Rarely**, **Not only** stoji pomožni glagol pred osebkom, kot v vprašanju. Pomeni isto kot **I have never seen such fog.** **Rarely do we get such a night.** **Not only did she get lost, but she also lost a shoe.** Tebi ni treba tako govoriti.
say.de: **Never have I seen such fog.** (Noch nie habe ich solchen Nebel gesehen.) Das erkennst du in Geschichten und Reden: Nach **Never**, **Rarely**, **Not only** steht das Hilfsverb vor dem Subjekt, wie in einer Frage. Es heißt dasselbe wie **I have never seen such fog.** **Rarely do we get such a night.** **Not only did she get lost, but she also lost a shoe.** Selbst musst du so nicht reden.
say.it: **Never have I seen such fog.** (Non ho mai visto una nebbia così.) Da riconoscere, nei racconti e nei discorsi: dopo **Never**, **Rarely**, **Not only** l'ausiliare viene prima del soggetto, come in una domanda. Vuol dire lo stesso di **I have never seen such fog.** **Rarely do we get such a night.** **Not only did she get lost, but she also lost a shoe.** Tu non hai bisogno di parlare così.
say.en: **Never have I seen such fog.** To recognise, in stories and speeches: after **Never**, **Rarely**, **Not only** the helping verb comes before the subject, as in a question. It says the same as **I have never seen such fog.** **Rarely do we get such a night.** **Not only did she get lost, but she also lost a shoe.** You needn't talk like that yourself.

translation.sl: V soboto se je teta Edna izgubila na hribu. Ustavila jo je megla. Našel jo je Jack, z Meg. Potrebovala je skodelico čaja. Gospa Birkett je vsem skuhala juho. »Tvoja juha mi je res všeč,« je rekla Edna. »Vem. Saj si to rekla že zadnjič,« je rekla gospa Birkett.
translation.de: Am Samstag hat sich Tante Edna am Berg verirrt. Der Nebel hat sie aufgehalten. Jack hat sie gefunden, mit Meg. Was sie brauchte, war eine Tasse Tee. Mrs Birkett kochte für alle Suppe. „Deine Suppe schmeckt mir wirklich“, sagte Edna. „Ich weiß. Das hast du schon letztes Mal gesagt“, sagte Mrs Birkett.
translation.it: È stato sabato che zia Edna si è persa in montagna. È stata la nebbia a fermarla. È stato Jack a trovarla, con Meg. Ciò di cui aveva bisogno era una tazza di tè. La signora Birkett ha fatto la zuppa per tutti. «La tua zuppa mi piace davvero», ha detto Edna. «Lo so. L'hai detto anche l'altra volta», ha detto la signora Birkett.
translation.en: It was on Saturday that Auntie Edna got lost on the fell. It was the fog that stopped her. It was Jack who found her, with Meg. What she needed was a cup of tea. What Mrs Birkett did was make soup for everybody. “I do like your soup,” said Edna. “I know. You did say so last time,” said Mrs Birkett.

exercises.text: It was Arthur ___ saved the bees. It was the cold ___ nearly killed them. What they needed ___ sugar. “You ___ look after them well,” said Mr Tyson.

accept: who
that
that
which
was
do
did
really
certainly
always

translation.sl: Čebele je rešil Arthur. Skoraj jih je pomoril mraz. Potrebovale so sladkor. »Res dobro skrbiš zanje,« je rekel gospod Tyson.
translation.de: Es war Arthur, der die Bienen gerettet hat. Die Kälte hätte sie fast umgebracht. Was sie brauchten, war Zucker. „Du kümmerst dich wirklich gut um sie“, sagte Mr Tyson.
translation.it: È stato Arthur a salvare le api. È stato il freddo a rischiare di ucciderle. Ciò di cui avevano bisogno era lo zucchero. «Te ne occupi davvero bene», ha detto il signor Tyson.
translation.en: It was Arthur who saved the bees. It was the cold that nearly killed them. What they needed was sugar. “You do look after them well,” said Mr Tyson.
